methods.formula: Total addressable market (TAM) for similar roles = Number of companies in industry × Average number of roles per company × Average compensation per role
variables: Number of companies in industry (e.g., software publishing)
Average number of senior engineers per company
Average total compensation per senior engineer
search_queries: number of software companies in US 2024
average number of senior engineers per tech company
average total compensation senior software engineer 2024
known_limitations: May overestimate if many companies are small

methods.formula: Market size = Sum over all known job postings of (Number of postings × Average compensation) for similar roles in relevant geography
variables: Number of job postings for similar roles (e.g., senior software engineer) in target region
Average compensation from postings or surveys
preferred_sources: Indeed, Glassdoor, LinkedIn job posting data
search_queries: senior software engineer job postings 2024 US
average salary for senior software engineer in [city] 2024
known_limitations: Job postings may not reflect actual hires
Compensation data may be self-reported and biased

methods.formula: Number of qualified candidates = Total labor force × Percentage with required skills × Percentage willing to relocate × Percentage accepting offer at given compensation
variables: Total labor force in relevant occupation (e.g., software developers)
Percentage with specific skills (e.g., AI, project management)
Offer acceptance rate at proposed compensation
search_queries: number of software developers in US 2024
percentage of developers with AI skills 2024
relocation acceptance rate tech jobs 2024

methods.formula: Total compensation value pool = Total revenue of industry × Average compensation as percentage of revenue
variables: Average compensation-to-revenue ratio for tech companies
search_queries: software industry revenue 2024
compensation as percentage of revenue tech companies 2024
known_limitations: Ratio varies widely by company size and profitability
May not reflect individual role compensation
